reason: E2 directly demonstrates the exact hybrid-rolling process on the same alloy, producing the claimed dual heterogeneous microstructure and reporting simultaneous strength (~2000 MPa) and ductility (~8%) improvements. E1 supports the mechanism by showing that a hierarchical lamellar architecture in this alloy enables microcrack-arresting and strength-ductility synergy, though it does not use the same processing route. Together, the evidence accurately supports all key premises.
premises: Cryo-rolling followed by warm-rolling at ~600°C can be applied to AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA to produce a nanostructured dual heterogeneous lamellar microstructure.
The dual heterogeneous microstructure increases back-stress and enhances strain hardening.
The refined interfaces and heterogeneity activate microcrack-arresting mechanisms, delaying catastrophic failure.
The hybrid processing simultaneously improves both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the as-cast baseline.
